candidate.answerReason: Three minutes is 180 seconds. The truck travels \(180b/(6t)=30b/t\) feet, which is \(10b/t\) yards.

methods.label: Find the rate and convert units
methods.explanation:
First express the travel time in seconds so it matches the given rate. Three minutes is \(3\cdot60=180\) seconds. Since \(t>0\) is the given time interval, the truck's rate is
\[
\frac{b/6}{t}=\frac{b}{6t}
\]
feet per second. Its distance in \(180\) seconds is therefore
\[
180\cdot\frac{b}{6t}=\frac{30b}{t}
\]
feet. There are \(3\) feet in each yard, so divide by \(3\):
\[
\frac{30b}{t}\div3=\frac{10b}{t}.
\]
The truck travels \(\frac{10b}{t}\) yards, choice E.
methods.levelReason: Unit conversion and distance equals rate times time require only elementary arithmetic and symbolic expressions.
